results.term_definition: Sirius, also called the Dog Star or Alpha Canis Majoris, is the star that appears brightest in the night sky to our eyes. It is located at a distance of 8.6 light years from us in the constellation Canis Major near Orion. The bright star that is visible to us is Sirius A, a star of spectral type A. Sirius A has a gravitationally bound companion, Sirius B, which is a white dwarf star that is very faint in visible light but very bright in X-rays. Sirius B is too faint and too close to Sirius A to be seen with the naked eye.
